quest.grege.bloodmagic10:
How to get this fruit?

1) Get a Ritual Diviner
2) Shift+Right Click it until it say Edge of the Hidden Realm
3) Make a Master Ritual Stone and some Ritual Stones
4) Right click the Master with Ritual Diviner to assemble the ritual.
5) Right click the Master with Ritual Activator (You need to have enough LP in your blood network - place Orb in a Altar to charge it)
6) Get inside the dungeon, unlock the doors with keys, and get a Tau Fruit
7) Place the Tau Fruit, then make a animal stand upon it, it will die and feed the fruit. You might need to repeat it a few times, the fruit damages the animal when it grows.
8) You can harvest the Saturated Tau Fruit now!
quest.grege.bloodmagic11:
How to get this?

Its similar to Tau Fruit, you need to find it in a dungeon.

1) Upgrade your Ritual Diviner to Ritual Diviner [Dusk]
2) Change it to Pathway to the Endless Realm ritual
3) Assemble the ritual and start it
4) Find special key (Foreman's or Miner's) in chests, then find the special room
5) Mine the ore! (you can double it)

quest.grege.explanation1: Behind this quest you will see some other quests teaching you how to work with GregTech.
quest.grege.explanation2:
GregTech machines have a circuit option in their GUI, so when you see a recipe with that circuit, you need to select it. That effectively locks the machine into making only the recipies with that circuit. Of course you can change the circuit later. For multiblocks you need to set the circuit in input bus/hatch.

Also you can make the number choosing circuit from a normal circuit.

Also also there is a AE2 addon that changes the circuit dynamically. Look into QOL quest chapter for more info.
quest.grege.explanation3: Probably the hardest thing about GregTech, because there will be a time when you will have to use BASIC MATH!!! So lets get into the explanation.
quest.grege.explanation4: First: Voltage. It's pretty straight forward, this tells you how much energy can pass through a cable. Every cable has different values, so read carefully!
quest.grege.explanation5: Second: Amperage. You can think about amperage as a package that unboxes to voltage. Amperages (or packages) are sent from a providers, like energy converters (they always send the amount of amperage that they have in their name, eg. LV 1A energy converter sends 1A. In LV, 1A = 32V, and this will scale up in every tier. Cables also have a maximum amperage that they allow, if you give them more, they WILL burn!
quest.grege.explanation6: Third: You can't tier skip cables, meaning if the cable doesn't say it can transport LV energy, then it really can't.
quest.grege.explanation7: You might have sees already that some recipes from GregTech have a different UI. It tells you the tier that you can craft the recipe, and also the exact time. If you click on the tier (eg. LV) you can change it so it shows you how would this recipe perform in other tiers.
quest.grege.explanation8: Energy converters convert FE to EU at a rate of 4:1. Solar panels are buffed so you can actually use them as a solid source of energy.
quest.grege.explanation9: Because converters in this pack defaultly convert to the correct state (transforming FE -> EU), you dont have to use soft mallet on them.
quest.grege.explanation10: This technology was brought to you by aliens from different Stars. Thank you Star Technology!
quest.grege.explanation11:
Each tier has its own superconducters, cables, which have no energy loss.

They are always locked behind the mod accompanying the chapter.
quest.grege.explanation12: You might be wondering how to get some of the Chiseled blocks. Well, you can craft the ones in the quest window and then you need to use Stonecutter from Minecraft to change them.
quest.grege.explanation13: My favourite part about every modpack: multiblocks, so I've tried to create at least 3 new per tier. Lets get into some tips about them!
quest.grege.explanation14:
Tip #1: There are multiple ways to preview the multiblock: in EMI, if you click on the controller, it will show you the layout. You can click on the blocks, it will tell you where you can put input busses, hatches, energy inputs, or parallel hatches.

When you decide where you wanna build your multiblock, place the controller and shift+right click it. It will show you the multiblock layout.

If you are really lazy, you can use the item 'Terminal' to build the multiblock for you. It will place hatches in random places, so you will have to change them to your liking.
quest.grege.explanation15:
Tip #2: If you open input busses, you can see that there are some options in bottom left. One is circuit and the other distinct bus.

1st option is about the recipes, like in singleblock machines.

2nd is more interesting, because this will allow you to basically use one multiblock for multiple recipes with different circuits. If you turn the option on, it will basically tell the multiblock, that this bus is different from the others, and the others can't access this inventory to use in crafting. This should be the default, but it is not so keep this in mind.
quest.grege.explanation16: Tip #3: Some multiblocks will have maintenance hatch, which you will need to repair when you first start working with the machine. Basically you need to click it with every GregTech tool, but later you will unlock tape that does it in one click and then a auto-maintenance hatch.
quest.grege.explanation17:
Tip #4: This is probably the most important one: OVERCLOCKING.

What you can do on some multiblocks is that you can place 2 energy hatches to 'overclock' the multiblock, basically doubling its speed.

This will save you a lot of time and also this is how you will unlock progress recipies, usually in Electric blast furnace, where you will need to use recipes 1 tier higher.

Also if you look at energy hatches, they are also in 4A, 16A variants, this will speed up the recipe too, but it will NOT overclock the machine, eg. you put 1 LV 4A energy hatch, it is still LV tier, even tho 4LV A = 1MV A. BUT you can place 2 LV 4A, and you are in MV tier!
quest.grege.explanation18:
Tip #5: When you hover over the multiblock controller, it can say it has some abilities.

Perfect Overclock - reduction of recipe time for recipes under the tier of the machine (LV recipe run in MV tier machine -> recipe time reduction on top of the 1/2 time from running LV on MV machine)

Abilities from the Greg-E-core mod: There are multiple of them, they are explained under the description of the machine.
quest.grege.explanation19:
Paralell hatches are used on big multiblock machines that unlock in LuV. It basically allows the multiblock to run 4 recipes at the same time with slight time reduction.

Basically get this as fast as possible.
quest.grege.explanation20: This item automatically builds your GregTech multiblocks.
quest.grege.explanation21:
Cu5tom Greg-E modifier, it allows machines to run 2 or more recipes in parallel. For example, you can have Steel Dust -> Steel Ingots on Thread 1, and at the same time Aluminium Dust -> Aluminium Ingots are running on Thread 2.

Basically multiple machines in 1.

It will still apply all the other boosts for the recipe.
quest.grege.ev1:
How to get to the nether:
1) Get 10 Titanium Blocks
2) Get EV robotic arm
3) Make a nether portal shape out of Titanium Blocks
4) Use the EV robotic arm as a lighter
5) You're in the nether!
quest.grege.ev2: Rare Earth has a production line now! You can upgrade your chances in every tier. This should help with those pesky Rare Earth rare materials!
quest.grege.ev3:
These hatches will start to unlock from EV.

How are they different from normal hatches? These send 4 Amps to a machine, meaning it will act as if you use 2 normal energy hatches. But! Using only 1 hatch will NOT overclock the machine, meaning you can only use recipes on tier with the energy hatch. If you use 2 hatches, it will overclock normally.

These come in 4, 8 and 16 Amp variants.

The fastest combo of hatches is using 2 16 Amp hatches, but if you don't have the energy generation, this will eat through your power.
quest.grege.goodstuff1:
These form the outer shell.

Frame blocks need to be on the edge, wall on the inside.

Hold G over the item to open the guide.
quest.grege.goodstuff2:
Core of the multiblock, can work on its own but when you make the full multiblock, gets so much better.

Maximum size is 7x7x7.
quest.grege.goodstuff3: Maximum of 5 in 1 matrix assembler, more does nothing.
quest.grege.goodstuff4: Each of these inside a Matrix Assembler adds 36 pattern spaces.
quest.grege.goodstuff5: Each of these can do 8 jobs at once.

Fun little production line :)

Also you get Small Piles of Nobelium, not the full dusts.

It simulates how Nobelium is created in real life.
quest.grege.hv4:
You kinda need to get helium for Nobelium, and there are 2 ways to get it:

a) This is easy to do but it yields low Helium
1) Craft Void Gas Extractor
2) Start extracting Natural Gasses and as a byproduct you get a bit of Helium

b) This gets you a lot of Helium but its more complicated:
1) Get T1 rocket and visit Moon
2) On moon you can get Desh (find 1 ore and then use mod Scannable to find others)
3) While searching for Desh, get Moon Cobblestone, which you can smelt to stone
4) Make a End Portal Frame block out of Moon Stone and Eye of Ender
5) You're in the End
6) Get Ender Air and distill it
quest.grege.hv5:
How to get AE2 channels in a cleanroom?

2 ways:

1) Place any machine hull in the Cleanroom wall, now it can act as a passthrough for a ME cable.

2) Wireless AE2: either Wireless Connectors from ExtendedAE or just the ol' reliable quantum ring.
quest.grege.hv6:
Huh, this seems familiar from a different universe...

Well, can't go wrong with good ideas.

Though, they don't have perfect overclock, its still good QOL.
quest.grege.hv7: This will help with component creation.
quest.grege.hv8:
By replacing the Filter Casings in the Cleanroom with these Filters, it will begin functioning as a Dimensional Simulator.

Next, add a Dimensional Relic Input and supply the required items to unlock the recipe. Once unlocked, you can insert any Gas Collector, allowing the recipe to be crafted regardless of the cleanroom's current dimension.

This is not needed, as the Gas Collectors will still work normally. This is just a QOL that can save some lag.

If you want to use this feature, and don't want to use a cleanroom, in LuV there is a multiblock called Anti-Mass Spectrometer, that offers this same functionality. But you need to add a Dimensional Simulator Maintenance Hatch to it.
quest.grege.hnn2:
This one, not so much.

Ultimate Simulation Chamber can only accept Extra Data Model (combined 4 models)
quest.grege.hnn3:
This machine can upgrade your models without giving you anything back. Why would you want to and not do it the original way? Because this is much faster, especially with the speed and data upgrades.

Now if you look at Chaos Guardian, it needs 32000 data. How to get there within normal time? Tier upgrade. That one uses so much energy but directly upgrades the model to next tier.
quest.grege.hnn4: With this machine you can combine 4 self-aware models to 1 model. It can be different mobs, but they all need to be self-aware. Then that model will be able to create 64 matrixes in 1 operation. Use Simulation Modeling to get it to best tier fast.

quest.grege.welcome1: Sup! Welcome to a skyblock modpack mainly focused on GregTech with unique material production featuring ProjectE.
quest.grege.welcome2: ProjectE has a somewhat bad name, that you can become OP really easily. Honestly, its not far from the truth, but here you can't really buy circuits with EMC. Those has to be crafted the normal way.
quest.grege.welcome3:
This pack will use EMC as a buying power. That means that all resources won't be mineable (you are on skyblock after all), but whats interesting is that there are always new ways to generate EMC in each tier.

In each new tier you will need to make a new alloy to sell for more EMC to buy more raw materials. I'll try to balance it to the best of my ability so you need to do every new generating line.
quest.grege.welcome4: Quests serve as a path that guides your progression, but you dont really have to complete them. You might have to experiment on your own.
